title: Priority-Based Ready Task Selection Plan
description: Implementation plan for changing automatic ready-task selection from traversal-order top-most popping to a deterministic priority tuple: depth ascending, child_count descending, shared_parent_count_with_current_task ascending.

scheduler.claimPolicy: Automatic claims must choose the best ready candidate by the deterministic priority tuple before creating a lease. Explicit node claims still require that the node is currently ready.

tuple.description: Prefer ready tasks closer to the root.
For equal depth, prefer the ready task with more outgoing edges.
For equal depth and child count, prefer the ready task that shares the fewest parent nodes with the current task.

selectionPolicy.tieBreaker: Use a stable final tie-breaker, such as node id or root path, so equal priority candidates remain deterministic.
selectionPolicy.currentTaskFallback: When there is no current task context, shared_parent_count_with_current_task is treated as 0 for every ready candidate.

scheduler.slackPolicy: Use chat for attention and approvals when configured. Canonical state remains in this graph file.

ROOT.title: Update scheduler ready-task selection
ROOT.description: First lock down the priority contract and baseline behavior. Then implement metadata, selection, current-task context, tests, and docs in parallel. Finally integrate and verify the scheduler as a whole.

DISCOVERY.title: Define contract and baseline
DISCOVERY.description: Make the intended behavior precise before touching scheduler mutation code.

PRIO1.title: Map current ready traversal and claim surfaces
PRIO1.description: Identify every place that observes, displays, or consumes ready nodes, especially listReadyLeafNodes, claimNode, worker prompt generation, diagnostics, visualizer payloads, and tests.
deliverables: A short implementation note naming the files and public outputs affected by ready ordering.
A list of behavior that must remain unchanged for explicit node claims, blocked nodes, expired leases, and subtree completion.
A decision on whether ready ordering should be centralized in traversal, claim selection, or a shared helper.
acceptanceCriteria: The plan accounts for CLI ready output, automatic claim output, diagnostics nextReady output, worker readyJson, and visualizer ready lists.
The current automatic claim behavior is confirmed to select the first ready candidate from traversal order.
No code behavior is changed in this task.

PRIO2.title: Specify priority semantics and tie-breakers
PRIO2.description: Write the exact scheduler contract for the tuple: depth ascending, child_count descending, shared_parent_count_with_current_task ascending, plus deterministic behavior for exact ties.
deliverables: A concise contract note in docs/compatibility-boundaries.md or a focused scheduler design note.
Definitions for depth, child_count, parent set, shared parent count, current task context, and no-current-task fallback.
A deterministic final tie-breaker that does not depend on object insertion quirks or worker timing.
acceptanceCriteria: Depth is defined as graph distance from root using the selected root path for valid reachable nodes.
Child count is defined as the ready candidate node's outgoing edge count, with leaf candidates naturally counting as 0.
Shared parent count is based on ancestor or direct-parent semantics explicitly chosen and documented.
The leaf-only claim model is either preserved with clear child_count implications or deliberately updated with compatibility notes.

PRIO3.title: Record baseline checks and priority fixture needs
PRIO3.description: Run the existing authoritative checks and sketch the fixture matrix needed to prove the new selection policy.
deliverables: Baseline results for npm run format:check, npm run typecheck, npm run build, and npm test.
A fixture matrix covering depth ordering, child count ordering, shared parent count ordering, explicit node claims, expired leases, and no-current-task fallback.
A note of any pre-existing failures or dirty working tree changes that should not be attributed to the priority work.
acceptanceCriteria: Baseline command results include exact pass/fail status and relevant error summaries.
The fixture matrix names expected winning node ids for each priority rule.
The implementation branches have enough context to write tests without re-litigating the contract.

PARALLEL_IMPLEMENTATION.title: Implement priority selection branches
PARALLEL_IMPLEMENTATION.description: Parallel work streams for graph-derived priority data, the comparator and claim behavior, current-task context, test coverage, and documentation.

GRAPH_METADATA.title: Graph metadata branch
GRAPH_METADATA.description: Compute priority inputs from the graph in one reusable place.

PRIO4.title: Add parent, depth, and path helpers
PRIO4.description: Implement helpers that derive parent sets, root depth, and stable root paths for reachable nodes without mutating the graph.
deliverables: Pure traversal helpers with typed return values.
Cycle-safe use of existing validated graph assumptions.
Stable behavior for duplicate ancestry, shared subgraphs, and unknown node kinds allowed by the current compatibility model.
acceptanceCriteria: Root depth is 0 and each reachable child depth is deterministic.
Nodes with multiple reachable paths receive the documented depth/path behavior.
Helpers are covered by unit tests before they are used by claim mutation code.

PRIO5.title: Compute ready candidate priority fields
PRIO5.description: Attach or derive depth, child_count, parent set, and shared_parent_count_with_current_task for each ready candidate.
deliverables: A candidate metadata model that can be reused by CLI, worker prompts, diagnostics, and visualizer payloads if the contract exposes priority data.
A shared-parent-count helper that accepts an optional current task id.
A clear distinction between internal helper fields and public JSON fields.
acceptanceCriteria: Child count is calculated from the candidate node's children array length, defaulting to 0.
Missing current task context produces equal shared parent counts without throwing.
Existing ReadyNode consumers continue to compile.

PRIO6.title: Harden metadata edge cases
PRIO6.description: Verify graph metadata helpers behave predictably on mixed series, parallel, gate, unknown-kind, shared-parent, and leaf-only graphs.
deliverables: Unit tests for metadata helper edge cases.
Assertions that invalid graphs are still rejected by validation before priority metadata is computed.
A compact comment or doc note explaining any surprising multiple-parent behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Metadata helpers do not change subtree readiness semantics.
Tests cover both shallow and deep ready nodes.
Tests cover a candidate with children if the contract permits non-leaf ready tasks.

SELECTION_POLICY.title: Selection policy branch
SELECTION_POLICY.description: Implement the deterministic comparator and wire it into automatic claims.

PRIO7.title: Implement priority comparator
PRIO7.description: Create a pure comparator for ready candidates using depth ascending, child_count descending, shared_parent_count_with_current_task ascending, then the final deterministic tie-breaker.
deliverables: Comparator tests that isolate each tuple component.
A stable final tie-breaker documented in test names.
No dependency on Date, lease timing, object enumeration side effects, or worker session order.
acceptanceCriteria: Lower depth wins over higher depth regardless of later tuple values.
Higher child_count wins when depth ties.
Lower shared_parent_count_with_current_task wins when depth and child_count tie.
Exact ties always sort in the same order across repeated runs.

PRIO8.title: Use priority ordering for automatic claims
PRIO8.description: Replace automatic selection of ready[0] with the best priority-ranked candidate while preserving explicit node claims and lease release behavior.
deliverables: claimNode automatic selection uses the priority-ranked ready set.
Expired claimed/running leases are still released before selection.
The claim result still reports the selected node id, title, run id, lease, releasedExpired, and summary.
acceptanceCriteria: Automatic claim picks the expected priority winner when multiple nodes are ready.
Explicit claim by node id succeeds only if that node is ready and does not re-rank to another node.
No ready node is double-claimed under concurrent automatic claims.

PRIO9.title: Align ready output surfaces
PRIO9.description: Decide and implement whether read-only ready surfaces should show priority-sorted order and optional priority metadata.
deliverables: Consistent ordering for CLI ready, diagnostics nextReady, worker readyJson, and visualizer ready lists if the public contract chooses sorted display.
Golden updates for any public JSON or text output changes.
Compatibility notes if new priority fields are exposed.
acceptanceCriteria: Every ready consumer observes either the same priority order or a documented intentionally different order.
Public JSON changes are covered by tests and docs.
Existing consumers that only read id, title, kind, and status remain compatible.

CURRENT_CONTEXT.title: Current task context branch
CURRENT_CONTEXT.description: Define and implement how shared_parent_count_with_current_task finds the currently running task.

PRIO10.title: Resolve current task source
PRIO10.description: Choose how automatic claim selection identifies the currently running task for shared-parent ranking.
deliverables: A documented resolver order, such as explicit currentTaskId option first, then an active claimed/running node for the same session, then no current task.
Behavior for zero, one, or multiple active tasks in the same session.
CLI and API compatibility notes for any new option or internal-only parameter.
acceptanceCriteria: The resolver never makes automatic claim nondeterministic when multiple active tasks exist.
No-current-task behavior matches the scheduler selectionPolicy metadata in this graph.
The worker flow can provide or infer current task context without breaking existing command shapes.

PRIO11.title: Wire current context into claim selection
PRIO11.description: Pass the resolved current task id into ready candidate scoring during automatic claim selection.
deliverables: claimNode and any lower-level helper accept the selected current task context.
Session-based current task inference is covered without changing explicit node claim semantics.
Errors mention invalid explicit current task context clearly if such an option is exposed.
acceptanceCriteria: The same ready graph can choose different candidates when current task context changes and the first two tuple fields tie.
Invalid or absent current context falls back safely.
Lease ownership and session attribution remain unchanged.

PRIO12.title: Exercise shared-parent ranking behavior
PRIO12.description: Create tests that prove candidates sharing fewer parents with the current task win after depth and child_count ties.
deliverables: A graph fixture where at least three ready candidates tie on depth and child_count but differ in shared parent count.
Tests for explicit current task id, inferred same-session current task, and no-current-task fallback.
Tests for deterministic behavior when shared parent counts tie.
acceptanceCriteria: The expected winner is asserted by node id for every shared-parent scenario.
The tests fail against traversal-order popping.
The tests pass independent of object key insertion order.

TEST_COVERAGE.title: Priority test branch
TEST_COVERAGE.description: Add regression coverage across unit, integration, CLI, and concurrency behavior.

PRIO13.title: Build priority fixture graphs
PRIO13.description: Create compact test graphs that isolate each priority tuple field while staying faithful to series-parallel readiness rules.
deliverables: A depth-priority graph where traversal order would choose a deeper node but priority chooses a shallower node.
A child-count-priority graph consistent with the finalized leaf-only or non-leaf candidate contract.
A shared-parent-priority graph with tied depth and child_count.
acceptanceCriteria: Each fixture has a readable expected winner.
Fixtures avoid unrelated statuses unless the test is specifically about blocked, failed, or expired leases.
Reusable fixture builders are preferred over checked-in JSON for one-off test cases.

PRIO14.title: Add scheduler integration tests
PRIO14.description: Cover automatic claim selection through the real graph mutation path, including leases, graph version increments, and persisted state.
deliverables: Integration tests for automatic claim winner selection.
Tests that explicit node claim remains opt-in and exact.
Tests that release-expired behavior still happens before priority selection.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests assert persisted graph status and lease data after selection.
A traversal-order implementation fails at least one new integration test.
Concurrent automatic claims still never return the same node id.

PRIO15.title: Update CLI and golden coverage
PRIO15.description: Update command-line, prompt, diagnostics, and golden tests for any ready ordering or public JSON shape changes.
deliverables: CLI ready output tests for priority order if read-only surfaces are sorted.
Worker prompt readyJson assertions that match the selected contract.
Golden fixture updates with stable ordering and no timestamp-sensitive expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: npm test covers the changed CLI-facing behavior.
Golden updates are limited to intentional priority-related changes.
Failure messages clearly distinguish priority ranking from readiness eligibility.

DOCS_COMPAT.title: Documentation and compatibility branch
DOCS_COMPAT.description: Document the new deterministic policy for operators and future maintainers.

PRIO16.title: Document operator-visible behavior
PRIO16.description: Update README and operator docs to explain how automatic claims choose among multiple ready tasks.
deliverables: README operating model update for the priority tuple.
Example that shows why a shallower ready task beats a deeper ready task.
Note that explicit node claims remain available for operator-directed work.
acceptanceCriteria: Docs use the exact tuple names: depth, child_count, shared_parent_count_with_current_task.
The docs mention deterministic tie-breaking.
The docs avoid implying workers can claim non-ready nodes.

PRIO17.title: Update compatibility boundaries
PRIO17.description: Record the priority policy as part of the public scheduler behavior and note any JSON output additions.
deliverables: docs/compatibility-boundaries.md names automatic claim ordering as stable behavior.
Any new ReadyNode fields are listed with compatibility expectations.
Any CLI option for current task context is documented with default behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Compatibility docs distinguish eligibility from priority ranking.
Breaking or additive changes are explicitly named.
Docs match the implemented fallback for missing current task context.

PRIO18.title: Add architecture notes for maintainers
PRIO18.description: Explain where priority metadata and comparison logic lives so future scheduling changes remain centralized.
deliverables: docs/architecture.md or a linked design note describing the helper boundaries.
Guidance for adding future tuple fields without scattering comparison logic.
A short note on why deterministic final tie-breaking matters for concurrent workers.
acceptanceCriteria: A maintainer can find the comparator and tests from the architecture note.
The note references existing traversal and mutation modules accurately.
No stale implementation paths are introduced.

INTEGRATION.title: Integrate and verify priority scheduling
INTEGRATION.description: Bring the branches together and prove the scheduler is coherent end to end.

PRIO19.title: Reconcile branch changes and public outputs
PRIO19.description: Review combined code, tests, docs, and JSON outputs for consistency across traversal, claim, worker, diagnostics, and visualizer surfaces.
deliverables: One integrated implementation path for computing and sorting ready candidates.
No duplicate priority comparators or drifting helper definitions.
A review note of any public output changes and why they are intentional.
acceptanceCriteria: All ready surfaces agree with the documented contract.
Explicit node claims and failure paths preserve existing error style.
TypeScript contracts remain narrow and documented.

PRIO20.title: Run authoritative checks
PRIO20.description: Run the repository's standard quality gates after integration.
deliverables: Passing npm run format:check.
Passing npm run typecheck.
Passing npm run build.
Passing npm test.
acceptanceCriteria: Any failure is either fixed or clearly documented with reproduction details.
No test is skipped solely to make the priority change pass.
Generated artifacts are not committed unless the repository already tracks them for this workflow.

PRIO21.title: Run migration smoke and manual sanity checks
PRIO21.description: Verify built entry points and realistic operator flows still work with the priority policy.
deliverables: Passing npm run smoke:migration or a documented environment-specific reason it cannot run.
Manual disposable-graph claim showing priority winner selection.
Optional visualizer sanity check if ready ordering is operator-visible there.
acceptanceCriteria: Built CLI entry points operate on both relative and absolute graph paths.
The smoke or manual claim proves traversal-order popping is no longer the automatic policy.
Visualizer or diagnostics output remains escaped and readable.

RELEASE.title: Prepare priority scheduler change for review
RELEASE.description: Package the completed change with evidence and clear review guidance.

PRIO22.title: Write final implementation summary
PRIO22.description: Summarize what changed, why the selection is deterministic, and what tests prove the new tuple behavior.
deliverables: A concise summary suitable for a pull request or handoff report.
Links or references to key comparator, traversal, claim, and test files.
A list of commands run and their results.
acceptanceCriteria: The summary names the exact priority tuple.
Residual risks or contract decisions are called out plainly.
The summary does not omit any failed or unrun verification command.

PRIO23.title: Review release readiness
PRIO23.description: Perform a final review for compatibility, determinism, concurrency, and operator documentation.
deliverables: A release-readiness checklist result.
Confirmation that docs and tests match the implemented policy.
A final go/no-go recommendation for merging the scheduler priority change.
acceptanceCriteria: No known blocker remains for the priority policy.
Any deferred enhancement is explicitly out of scope.
The graph can be reconciled cleanly after all tasks are complete.
